newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-ACT MOVE TOP WITH STYLISH DEMOLITION.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-ACT MOVE TOP WITH STYLISH DEMOLITION.

text.p: Australian Capital Territory moved one point clear at the top of the Super 12 standings on Saturday after humiliating New South Wales 56-9 with a stunning display of attacking rugby.

ACT are set to be overtaken by either Auckland or Natal who meet at Eden Park on Sunday, but thrilled a record crowd at Bruce Stadium by scoring eight tries to nil against their wealthier compatriots.
Fly-half David Knox orchestrated an inventive ACT backline superbly, launching a succession of precise raids to utterly demoralise the hapless and outclassed visitors.
The former Wallaby, discarded by New South Wales two seasons ago, scored one try and kicked five conversions and two penalties in a gratifying personal haul of 21 points.
With scrum-half George Gregan thoroughly outplaying his New South Wales counterpart and Australia test rival Sam Payne -- and scoring one try into the bargain -- ACT enjoyed a wealth of possession.
Wingers Joe Roff and Mitch Hardy capitalised on the speed of movement and accurate passing in midfield to score two tries each.
Such was their domination, the home side earned a competition bonus point for scoring four or more tries after only 30 minutes in a blistering opening and led 29-9 at halftime.
Prop Patricio Noriega and centre James Holbeck crossed the line inside the first five minutes to delight a crowd of 18,753 -- a record attendance for a rugby union match in Canberra.
New South Wales were restricted to three penalties from the boot of Wallaby full-back Matthew Burke in a woeful team performance.

Missing four regulars, including suspended prop Richard Harry and injured winger David Campese, they looked ponderous and predictable in attack, while their forwards were easily contained by the ACT pack.
The unheralded Brumbies, in contrast, threatened to score every time they had possession during the second half.
Following their away win in Queensland earlier in the season, ACT have established themselves as Australia's leading province despite being dwarfed in terms of size and population by their rivals.

New South Wales - Matt Burke, Alistair Murdoch, Graeme Bond, Richard Tombs, Chris Latham, Scott Bowen, Sam Payne, Tim Gavin (captain), Daniel Manu, Stu Pinkerton, John Welborn, Sam Domoni, Andrew Heath, Mark Bell, Cameron Blades.

ACT - Stephen Larkham, Mitch Hardy, James Holbeck, Pat Howard, Joe Roff, David Knox, George Gregan, Troy Coker, Brett Robinson (captain), Owen Finegan, David Giffin, John Langford, Ewen McKenzie, Marco Caputo, Patricio Noriega.
